findings.location: AD-5 and AD-11, lines 205-211 and 253-261; data-model.md Business Logic Document publication, lines 297-303
findings.affected_requirement: Spec FR-012, FR-035, FR-037 and SC-009; Constitution II Document immutability and Version Chain
findings.evidence: AD-5 defines the Flow Group identity over the Pass 1 pair execution in addition to the endpoint-centered fields. AD-11 and the data model then key the stable Logical Document by the 'stable endpoint-centered group key' without defining a separate cross-scan key or persistence field, while also promising that a later pair completion appends a successor to the same Logical Document. If the only defined group identity is used, every new pair execution produces a different Logical Document and cannot form the promised Version Chain; if a different key is intended, its exact preimage, uniqueness, migration shape, and replay/current-pointer behavior are absent.
findings.correction_outcome: Define two explicit canonical identities: an execution-instance Flow Group identity that may include the pair execution, and a cross-scan Logical Document stable key derived only from durable endpoint-centered semantic identity. Specify the stable key preimage, normalization/schema-version evolution rule, consumer-entry stability across Code Logic Document Versions, uniqueness constraint, current-pointer concurrency, exact replay, changed endpoint behavior, and tests proving a later pair appends/supersedes rather than creates an unrelated Logical Document.

findings.location: CurrentCommunicationCandidate in data-model.md lines 9-28 and Resolution algorithm steps 1-3
findings.affected_requirement: Spec FR-005, FR-007, FR-008 and SC-001/SC-002; Story 12.4 AC-1
findings.evidence: The contract creates evidence-granular Provider candidates with classification, Source Anchor, catalog rule and Evidence Locator identity, then treats 'more than one Provider' in one protocol/key bucket as multiple providers. The accepted requirement is exactly one unique current provider Document Version, not exactly one provider evidence occurrence. Two valid locators or classifications that reproduce the same endpoint in the same current provider XML Document Version therefore become two candidates and can be misclassified as multiple providers, while the plan defines neither a provider-equivalence key nor aggregation of all evidence for one provider owner.
findings.correction_outcome: Define provider uniqueness over an explicit current provider identity, at minimum the current provider XML Document Version plus its Repository/System/revision binding, while retaining every contributing candidate as reproducibility evidence. Canonically collapse duplicate observations for that same provider identity before the sole-provider count; preserve ambiguity when distinct provider Document Versions remain; fingerprint and persist the complete aggregated evidence set; and add randomized vectors for duplicate locators/classifications in one provider versus two distinct provider Documents.

summary: REVISE. The plan is otherwise feasible and well aligned on deterministic exact matching, bounded endpoint-centered planning, closed retrieval, atomic publication, replay, security, migration compatibility, qualification, and Story 12.5 exclusions. Two High plan-owned identity gaps prevent task generation: the current group/stable-Document identity cannot prove cross-scan Version Chains, and evidence-granular Provider candidates can turn one unique provider Document Version into a false multiple-provider outcome. All three declared AGENTS.md triggers are accurate: the Scan strategy changes, the new Worker Agent tools retrieve_code_logic and submit_business_logic, and the dated FR-4.5/FR-6.1/FR-6.2 replacement each require explicit planned-change authorization after a corrected independent plan-review ACCEPT and before tasks. No authorization should be requested against this revised boundary. The nonrecursive boundary identity is SHA-256 over sorted path-tab-file-SHA256 lines for the nine pinned raw definition artifacts.
